title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
abstract: arXiv:2610.26836v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM agents that compute the right answer can still answer wrongly. Agent harnesses increasingly keep long tool outputs out of the context window, saving them to files that the agent searches or reads on demand. We ask where this costs accuracy with a real scientific tool: PHREEQC, a widely used geochemistry simulator from the USGS, whose reports reach 846.8k characters and whose determinism lets every printed value be traced. Agents use it to answer 158 execution-verified multiple-choice items. When agents read the simulator's report through a section index rather than in context, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 lose 11.3 and 7.9 points of accuracy, while Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 show no detectable cost. Re-running all 11,007 logged simulator calls shows that both GPT models compute the keyed value about as often as before; what changes is the evidence they answer from. translated_title: 相同的模拟，不同的证据：检索式工具输出在何处损害LLM智能体的准确性
translated_abstract: 即使计算出了正确答案，LLM智能体仍可能给出错误的回答。智能体框架越来越多地将长工具输出排除在上下文窗口之外，转而保存到文件中供智能体按需搜索或读取。我们借助一个真实的科学工具来探究这种做法在何处损害准确性：PHREEQC，这是美国地质调查局（USGS）广泛使用的地球化学模拟器，其报告可长达84.68万字符，且其确定性使每一个打印出的数值都可被追溯。智能体使用该工具回答158道经执行验证的选择题。当智能体通过章节索引而非上下文阅读模拟器报告时，GPT-5.1和GPT-5.2分别损失11.3和7.9个百分点的准确率，而Claude Opus 4.6和Claude Sonnet 4.6则未表现出可检测的代价。重新运行全部11,007次记录在案的模拟器调用表明，两个GPT模型计算出标准答案值的频率与之前大致相同；发生变化的是它们回答时所依据的证据。在检索模式下，它们常常跳过报告，转而依据自己的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文利用确定性的PHREEQC地球化学模拟器实验发现，当长工具输出被移出上下文、改为按需检索时，GPT-5.1和GPT-5.2的准确率分别下降11.3和7.9点而Claude模型不受影响，其根本原因并非计算出错，而是GPT模型在检索模式下跳过模拟报告、不再以模拟证据作为回答依据。
en_tdlr: Using the deterministic PHREEQC geochemistry simulator, this paper reveals that retrieving long tool outputs from files instead of keeping them in context costs GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 11.3 and 7.9 points of accuracy while Claude models are unaffected—not because they compute wrong values, but because under retrieval they skip the simulator report and answer from different evidence.
